meta.title: Held claims: submitted claims not (yet) on the map
meta.notes: Claims from submissions that were not added to the map. status needs_source = no source found yet; a source can promote it to an edge. status misleading = sources point the other way; kept so it can be revisited. raised_in lists the issue numbers that made the claim, so repeats are counted. Not loaded by the map. raised_in may also name a research branch (e.g. 'grok-v1 branch') instead of an issue number.

statuses.needs_source: No source found that confirms the claim. Send a direct link to promote it.
statuses.misleading: Available sources contradict or do not support the claim as worded.
statuses.promoted: A source now supports the claim; it is mapped in the lead file named in 'checked'. Kept here for the record.

claims.claim: Batory paid Iustitia 95,000 zł in 2019 for outreach at music festivals and book fairs
claims.checked: Batory's 2019 annual report; only a summary of page 23 could be read, which matches the claim. Needs a word-for-word check of page 23. Second pass 2026-10-31: the entry 'Stowarzyszenie Sędziów Polskich IUSTITIA, Warszawa / 95 000 zł' (human-rights and constitution education, music festivals and book fairs) is reported again on about p. 23, but only through a summary of the PDF; still no word-for-word read. Whether it is a competition or non-competition grant is unclear.

claims.claim: Batory gave Iustitia a EUR 50,000 institutional grant in 2022
claims.checked: Batory 2022 annual report pp. 1-37: only a EUR 22,319 project instalment found. The per-grant list of institutional grants was not reached. Re-checked 2026-10-31: still no Iustitia institutional entry in the 2022 report. Second pass 2026-10-31: the 2022 report says 23 institutional grants of EUR 50-100k were made (EUR 2,257,835 in total) but does not name recipients in the pages read. The only Iustitia line found is the EUR 22,319 thematic instalment (already mapped). No Iustitia institutional grant found in the 2022 financial statement either.

claims.claim: The Foundation to Promote Open Society gives Batory about 6.3 million zł a year and is its largest donor
claims.checked: Batory 2019 and 2022 reports name the Open Society donor but give no amounts. Financial statements not yet checked. Second pass 2026-10-31: the 'about 6.3 million zł a year' figure matches no year read. The 2024 financial statement (p. 21, read word for word) lists FPOS at PLN 15,979,870 in 2024, the largest donor line; that edge is now in lead_held_claims_sources.json. Partial reads (not word for word) give FPOS PLN 4,084,232 in 2022 and PLN 1,527,059 in 2020, with a separate Swiss Open Society entity at PLN 1,410,557 (2022) and PLN 2,919,658 (2020). The amount swings widely, so a flat yearly figure misleads.

claims.claim: The Aequitas judges' association published a tally of Batory money to Iustitia: EUR 156,958 + 95,000 zł
claims.checked: Aequitas document not found. Parts of the tally match Batory reports (2023 EUR 44,639 + 40,000 already on the map; 2022 EUR 22,319 confirmed). Second pass 2026-10-31: still no Aequitas document found by search.

claims.claim: Berek said the Sejm-elected judges have a prepared plan to restore the Tribunal using existing statutory tools, and would not reveal it in advance
claims.checked: Not in OKO.press (11 and 30 Aug 2026) or Interia coverage of his Sejm committee hearing. Sejm committee transcript not checked. Second pass 2026-10-31: no source has Berek himself saying this. Checked the 4 Sep 2026 Sejm transcript (point 22; Berek does not speak), Interia (anonymous government sources speak of a plan to 'take back' the TK, mapped as alleged), OKO.press 30 Aug (paywalled, nothing visible) and the judges' joint statement of 16 Oct 2026 ('all actions provided by law' to restore the Tribunal, mapped as fact). Nothing about keeping a plan secret.

claims.claim: Piotr Serafin, as gatekeeper, unlocked about EUR 137 billion of frozen EU funds for Poland after the 2023 change of government
claims.checked: PAP (18 Sep 2024) calls him gatekeeper for blocking funds under the rule-of-law conditionality mechanism as Budget Commissioner. No source found tying him personally to the unlocking or to the EUR 137bn figure. His tie to Tusk (chief aide 2014-19) is already on the map.

claims.claim: PhD supervisors: Dziurda - Tadeusz Ereciński (UW 2004); Taborowski - Władysław Czapliński (INP PAN 2011)
claims.checked: Polish Wikipedia could not be reached from the checking tool (not missing); no second source found yet. Markiewicz (Zedler) and Berek (Zubik) are now on their profiles. Second pass 2026-10-31: Taborowski's Sejm candidacy print 2338 and RPO page confirm a doctorate and a 2020 habilitation but give no PhD year, place or supervisor (birth data now mapped). Dziurda's print 2332 has a cover page only; sakig.pl gives no PhD details. Polish Wikipedia still unreachable from the checking tool (not missing).

claims.claim: Bio details: Bentkowska born 24 Nov 1966, daughter of Aleksander Bentkowski, DePaul scholarship; Berek ENA study and 2005 PO Sejm candidacy; Szostek PhD 2003 and Horizon 2020 grants SHOP4CF and MAS4AI; Korwin-Piotrowska's SGH postgraduate years 2004 and 2014
claims.checked: Polish Wikipedia could not be reached from the checking tool (not missing); no second source found yet. Markiewicz's and Berek's birth data, Berek's minister posts, Szostek's birth date and Bentkowska's Rzeszów roots are now on their profiles. Second pass 2026-10-31: Sejm candidacy prints for Bentkowska (2331), Dziurda (2332), Korwin-Piotrowska (2333), Markiewicz (2335) and Szostek (2337) are cover pages only; no CVs. Szostek: CORDIS lists the University of Silesia in MAS4AI (EU EUR 203,125) but not in SHOP4CF, and neither names him, so the SHOP4CF part looks wrong. Szostek's habilitation was at Wrocław (us.edu.pl); PhD year not found. Berek's ENA study and 2005 candidacy, Bentkowska's birth date/father/DePaul, Korwin-Piotrowska's SGH years: no second source yet.

claims.claim: Markiewicz spoke at Batory's Nov 2024 conference on a year of rebuilding the rule of law
claims.checked: Batory's 2024 annual report, the cited source, does not name him or the conference. Second pass 2026-10-31: Batory's event page lists Markiewicz (as Iustitia president) on Panel 1 of the 28-29 Nov 2024 Batory/HFHR conference. Mapped in lead_held_claims_sources.json. It is a programme listing, not an attendance record.

claims.claim: Batory paid for repair of the Tour de Konstytucja bus in its 3rd edition
claims.checked: Cited Wyborcza article could not be read (blocked). Batory's 2024 report does show a PLN 154,000 grant to Fundacja Aktywna Demokracja, now on the map. Second pass 2026-10-31: Wyborcza still blocks automated reading; no other coverage found.

claims.claim: USAID cooperative agreement 7200AA22CA00025 (about $6.4m) funds Dexis's Central Europe rule-of-law programme
claims.checked: HigherGov lists the $6,389,705 agreement as 'Building Resilience in Civil Society' to undisclosed foreign awardees, which matches GMF's CEBRICS title, and never mentions Dexis.

claims.claim: Batory/EEA money to Themis: PLN 2,389.98 (2016) and PLN 154,989.98 under Active Citizens
claims.checked: Source is an MP's X post that could not be read; the Themis project page failed. The 2014 EEA project itself is on the map. Second pass 2026-10-31: no Themis line in Batory's 2019, 2020, 2022 or 2024 reports/statements as read; the Active Citizens project database cannot be searched from a static page; themis-sedziowie.eu has no projects page.

claims.claim: HFHR received money from GMF's CEBRICS 2023 portfolio
claims.checked: The CEBRICS factsheet names HFHR as an implementation partner, not as a grantee. The partner tie is on the map.

claims.claim: Latarnik Wyborczy was part of a PKO/Orlen-backed 'manipulative campaign'
claims.checked: Cited warsawpoint.com page could not be read. GMF credits the Center for Citizenship Education's 'Electoral Lighthouse' app; that tie is on the map. Second pass 2026-10-31: warsawpoint.com page still unreadable (client error).

claims.claim: Kuisz is president of the Kultura Liberalna Foundation; Wigura is its co-founder
claims.checked: KRS page failed; the site's 'about' page lists Kuisz as editor-in-chief only and says nothing about co-founders. Second pass 2026-10-31: the foundation's own page names Kuisz as prezes zarządu and Wigura (Karolina Jadwiga Wigura-Kuisz) as board member; both mapped. Still unsourced: that Wigura is a co-founder.

claims.claim: Journal of Democracy is NED's in-house journal
claims.checked: NED's International Forum produces the journal and Johns Hopkins University Press publishes it 'for the Endowment'. 'In-house' overstates it; mapped with that wording.

claims.claim: At the Dom Sędziego Seniora founding, Iustitia was represented by Maciej Strączyński and Jolanta Korwin-Piotrowska, Themis by Irena Kamińska
claims.checked: The foundation page lists founders and Kamińska as board vice-president but not who represented each founder; Kwartalnik Iustitia lists Jolanta Korwin-Piotrowska on the first council only. No family tie to Anna Korwin-Piotrowska is documented. Not re-checked in the second pass.

claims.claim: The prosecutor's statement reproduces Patyra's panel allegations for TK cases K 3/26, Kpt 1/26, U 2/26 and K 22/26
claims.checked: The 1 Oct 2026 prosecutor statement names no TK case numbers and no specific panels. The case list may come from another document; none was cited.

claims.claim: On 30 Oct 2026 Korwin-Piotrowska issued a separate order imposing a one-month break in duties on Vice-President Sochański
claims.checked: The TK information page title names both Święczkowski and Sochański, but the page and the order PDFs could not be read (blocked). Needs a readable copy or press report. Second pass 2026-10-31: rp.pl (PAP), TVN24 and Interia report a one-month break for both Święczkowski and Sochański on 30 Oct 2026. Mapped in lead_held_claims_sources.json.

claims.claim: The 30 Oct order invokes art. 12(4)/11(2) TK Act, art. 130(1) common courts law, art. 10(1) Supreme Court Act and art. 19/30 TK judges status act, and lists seven grounds (assembly and 2027 budget, five judges not admitted, ECHR interim measure of 5 May 2026, outsiders at Berek's oath, political statements, panel order, delays)
claims.checked: Order PDFs blocked to automated reading. The map already carries Patyra's note giving the main reasons. Needs a readable copy. Second pass 2026-10-31: partly confirmed and mapped: art. 130 common courts law via art. 19 status act and art. 10 § 1 SN Act; art. 12(4) TK Act for the stand-in; reasons include the 2027 spending plan/General Assembly, panel assignments, and non-admission of judges since 9 Apr 2026 against the ECHR order of 5 May 2026. Still unsourced: art. 11(2) TK Act, art. 30 status act, and the reasons 'outsiders at Berek's oath', 'political statements' and 'delays' (delays came up only in a separate statement). The order text itself is still unread.

claims.claim: NIK (Supreme Audit Office) put funding for the PFN system at PLN 633m+ through 2026
claims.checked: Not in the Polsat (15 Jul 2026) or OKO.press (2017) articles. The cited Polskie Radio article could not be read. Second pass 2026-10-31: PLN 633.75m is Bankier.pl's own sum of the founding-act payment schedule through 2026 (4 Sep 2024), not a NIK figure. NIK's figure (16 Jan 2024) is PLN 152m to PFN from nine audited state companies in 2017-2021; that is now mapped.

claims.claim: PLN 8.43m is the amount of the Fair Courts campaign
claims.checked: Prosecutors give 'at least PLN 8.4m' as alleged damage to PFN, not the campaign cost. OKO.press put the campaign budget at about PLN 10m.

claims.claim: Former Solvere board members Anna P. and Piotr M. were detained in the PFN investigation
claims.checked: TVP (23 Sep 2026) confirms CBA detained 'Piotr M. and Anna P.' on the Rzeszów prosecutor's order, but does not name Solvere. Linking them to Solvere is an inference from founders' initials. Private individuals: not mapped without a source naming the link. Second pass 2026-10-31: OKO.press and PAP (via superbiz.se.pl) name the two detainees as former Solvere board members. Mapped as alleged, with initials only.

claims.claim: Elon Musk reshared (with a 🤔) a post claiming Biden-era USAID money went to anti-PiS groups in Poland
claims.checked: The reshare itself is documented (27 Feb 2025), but Musk made no claim of his own and the original post's evidence for USAID money reaching anti-PiS groups was not traced. Removed from the map on 2026-10-31 (was a fact line Musk -> Tusk, and Musk was ringed as US government because he ran DOGE as a special government employee). Promote back only if the original post's underlying grant records are found.

removed_edge.relation: reshared a post (with 🤔) claiming Biden-era USAID money went to anti-PiS groups; made no claim himself
